verses.m: “ ‘Incensed to see me lacerated at both the breasts, and hissing like a venomous serpent, he then spoke as follows: ‘By whom have your breasts been actually wounded, O lady with thighs resembling the proboscis of an elephant? Who is playing with an angry five-headed serpent?’ (24-25)

verses.text:
वीक्षमाणस्ततस्तं वै वायसं समवैक्षत।
नखैः सरुधिरैस्तीक्ष्णैर्मामेवाभिमुखं स्थितम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: “ ‘Gazing all round, he thereupon actually perceived that crow sitting with its face turned towards me alone, its sharp claws stained with blood. (26)

verses.text:
पुत्रः किल स शक्रस्य वायसः पततां वरः।
धरान्तरं गतः शीघ्रं पवनस्य गतौ समः॥ २७॥
verses.m: “ ‘That crow, the foremost of birds, was, they say, no other than the son of Indra (the ruler of gods), who had quickly descended from the heaven to the earth, vying as he did with the wind in speed. (27)

verses.text:
ततस्तस्मिन् महाबाहुः कोपसंवर्तितेक्षणः।
वायसे कृतवान् क्रूरां मतिं मतिमतां वरः॥ २८॥
verses.m: “ ‘His eyes rolling through fury, the mighty-armed prince, the foremost of the wise, made a severe resolve with regard to that crow. (28)

verses.text:
स दर्भसंस्तराद् गृह्य ब्रह्मणोऽस्त्रेण योजयत्।
स दीप्त इव कालाग्निर्जज्वालाभिमुखो द्विजम्॥ २९॥
verses.m: “ ‘Taking a blade of the sacred Kuśa grass from his mat, he charged it with the potency of the mystic missile presided over by Brahmā (the creator). It burst into flames like the blazing fire of universal destruction before the bird. (29)

verses.text:
स तं प्रदीप्तं चिक्षेप दर्भं तं वायसं प्रति।
ततस्तु वायसं दर्भः सोऽम्बरेऽनुजगाम ह॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “ ‘He hurled that fiery blade of the sacred Kuśa grass at the aforesaid crow. Presently that blade of the sacred Kuśa grass for its part actually followed the crow through the air. (30)

verses.text:
अनुसृष्टस्तदा काको जगाम विविधां गतिम्।
त्राणकाम इमं लोकं सर्वं वै विचचार ह॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “ ‘Seeking protection when given chase to by the missile, the crow then sought various asylums and thus actually ranged this whole universe: so it is said. (31)

verses.text:
स पित्रा च परित्यक्तः सर्वैश्च परमर्षिभिः।
त्रीँल्लोकान् सम्परिक्रम्य तमेव शरणं गतः॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “ ‘Having duly traversed through all the three worlds (the earth, heaven and the region lying between them), nay, deserted by his father Indra and all the greatest Ṛṣis, he sought Śrī Rāma alone as his refuge. (32)

verses.text:
स तं निपतितं भूमौ शरण्यः शरणागतम्।
वधार्हमपि काकुत्स्थः कृपया पर्यपालयत्॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “ ‘Out of compassion the celebrated Śrī Rāma (a scion of Kakutstha), spared the crow, who had sought pardon from him and fallen on the ground, though deserving of death. (33)

verses.text:
परिद्यूनं विवर्णं च पतमानं तमब्रवीत्।
मोघमस्त्रं न शक्यं तु ब्राह्मं कर्तुं तदुच्यताम्॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “ ‘Even as he was falling, Śrī Rāma said to the crow, whose energy had exhausted and who had grown pale through fear : ‘The missile presided over by Brahmā cannot in any case be rendered ineffectual : it may, therefore, be pointed out how to make it effectual.’ (34)

verses.text:
ततस्तस्याक्षि काकस्य हिनस्ति स्म स दक्षिणम्।
दत्त्वा तु दक्षिणं नेत्रं प्राणेभ्यः परिरक्षितः॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “ ‘Then Śrī Rāma destroyed the right eye of the crow. Since he had actually sacrificed his right eye, he was spared his life. (35)

verses.text:
स रामाय नमस्कृत्वा राज्ञे दशरथाय च।
विसृष्टस्तेन वीरेण प्रतिपेदे स्वमालयम्॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “ ‘Having made obeisance to Śrī Rāma and mentally to his father, King Daśaratha, when dismissed by that hero, he returned to his abode. (36)

verses.text:
मत्कृते काकमात्रेऽपि ब्रह्मास्त्रं समुदीरितम्।
कस्माद् यो माहरत् त्वत्तः क्षमसे तं महीपते॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “ ‘Addressing Śrī Rāma again, as though present before her, ‘a missile presided over by Brahmā was discharged by you at a mere crow for my sake. How then, O ruler of the earth, do you bear with him who wrested me from you? (37)

verses.text:
स कुरुष्व महोत्साहां कृपां मयि नरर्षभ।
त्वया नाथवती नाथ ह्यनाथा इव दृश्यते॥ ३८॥
verses.m: “ ‘Such that you are, pray show compassion to me with great vigour, O jewel among men ! She, who has her lord in you, O lord, actually looks like one without any protector. (38)

verses.text:
आनृशंस्यं परो धर्मस्त्वत्त एव मया श्रुतम्।
जानामि त्वां महावीर्यं महोत्साहं महाबलम्॥ ३९॥
अपारवारमक्षोभ्यं गाम्भीर्यात् सागरोपमम्।
भर्तारं ससमुद्राया धरण्या वासवोपमम्॥ ४०॥
verses.m: “ ‘From you alone have I heard that motiveless compassion is the highest virtue. Nay, I know you to be endowed with extraordinary valour, extraordinary vigour and extraordinary might, limitless in time or space, incapable of being disturbed and resembling the ocean in profundity, the lord of the earth, including the oceans and a compeer of Indra, the lord of paradise. (39-40)

verses.text:
एवमस्त्रविदां श्रेष्ठो बलवान् सत्त्ववानपि।
किमर्थमस्त्रं रक्षःसु न योजयसि राघव॥ ४१॥
verses.m: “ ‘Wherefore, O scion of Raghu, do you not employ your missiles against the ogres, even though you are, as aforesaid, the foremost of those proficient in the use of missiles, mighty and full of courage?’ ” (41)

verses.text:
न नागा नापि गन्धर्वा न सुरा न मरुद्गणाः।
रामस्य समरे वेगं शक्ताः प्रतिसमीहितुम्॥ ४२॥
verses.m: Turning to Hanumān “Neither Nāgas nor Gandharvas (celestial musicians), nor gods nor the Māruts (the fory-nine wind-gods) are able to resist the onrush of Śrī Rāma in combat. (42)

verses.text:
तस्य वीर्यवतः कच्चिद् यद्यस्ति मयि सम्भ्रमः।
किमर्थं न शरैस्तीक्ष्णैः क्षयं नयति राक्षसान्॥ ४३॥
verses.m: “If there still exists any regard for me in the heart of that powerful prince, wherefore does he not destroy the ogres with his sharp arrows? (43)

verses.text:
भ्रातुरादेशमादाय लक्ष्मणो वा परंतपः।
कस्य हेतोर्न मां वीरः परित्राति महाबलः॥ ४४॥
verses.m: “Or, why does not the heroic Lakṣmaṇa, the scourge of the foes, nay, who is endowed with extraordinary might, deliver me, taking permission of his eldest brother? (44)

verses.text:
यदि तौ पुरुषव्याघ्रौ वाय्विन्द्रसमतेजसौ।
सुराणामपि दुर्धर्षौ किमर्थं मामुपेक्षतः॥ ४५॥
verses.m: “If those two tigers among men, who are equal to Indra and the wind-god in energy, are difficult to overcome even by gods, wherefore do they disregard me? (45)

verses.text:
ममैव दुष्कृतं किंचिन्महदस्ति न संशयः।
समर्थावपि तौ यन्मां नावेक्षेते परंतपौ॥ ४६॥
verses.m: “Some major sin of mine alone comes in the way in that those twin scourges of their foes, do not take care of me, even though they are capable to do so: there is no doubt about it.” (46)

verses.text:
वैदेह्या वचनं श्रुत्वा करुणं साश्रु भाषितम्।
अथाब्रवीन्महातेजा हनूमान् हरियूथपः॥ ४७॥
त्वच्छोकविमुखो रामो देवि सत्येन ते शपे।
रामे दुःखाभिपन्ने तु लक्ष्मणः परितप्यते॥ ४८॥
verses.m: Hearing the aforesaid piteous appeal uttered by Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory, with tears in her eyes, Hanumān, a leader of monkey hordes, who was endowed with extraordinary energy, forthwith replied as follows: “I swear to you by truth, O godlike lady, that Śrī Rāma has grown averse to everything else through grief caused by your absence. And Lakṣmaṇa too suffers agony due to Śrī Rāma being overwhelmed with sorrow. (47-48)

verses.text:
कथंचिद् भवती दृष्टा न कालः परिशोचितुम्।
इमं मुहूर्तं दुःखानामन्तं द्रक्ष्यसि शोभने॥ ४९॥
verses.m: “Somehow you have been discovered by me; hence this is not the time for grieving. From this very hour you will see the end of your woes drawing near, O glorious lady ! (49)

verses.text:
तावुभौ पुरुषव्याघ्रौ राजपुत्रौ महाबलौ।
त्वद्दर्शनकृतोत्साहौ लोकान् भस्मीकरिष्यतः॥ ५०॥
verses.m: “Both the aforesaid princes, who are tigers among men and are endowed with extraordinary might, and who are determined to see you, will reduce all the ogres to ashes. (50)

verses.text:
हत्वा च समरक्रूरं रावणं सहबान्धवम्।
राघवस्त्वां विशालाक्षि स्वां पुरीं प्रति नेष्यति॥ ५१॥
verses.m: “Nay, killing Rāvaṇa, who is ferocious on the field of battle, along with his kinsfolk, Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, O large-eyed lady, will take you back to his own city. (51)

verses.text:
ब्रूहि यद् राघवो वाच्यो लक्ष्मणश्च महाबलः।
सुग्रीवो वापि तेजस्वी हरयो वा समागताः॥ ५२॥
verses.m: “Now, please communicate what message is to be delivered by me on your behalf to Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) as well as to Lakṣmaṇa, who is endowed with extraordinary might, or even to Sugrīva, who is full of energy, or to the monkeys assembled at Kiṣkindhā.” (52)

verses.text:
इत्युक्तवति तस्मिंश्च सीता पुनरथाब्रवीत्।
कौसल्या लोकभर्तारं सुषुवे यं मनस्विनी॥ ५३॥
तं ममार्थे सुखं पृच्छ शिरसा चाभिवादय।
स्रजश्च सर्वरत्नानि प्रियायाश्च वराङ्गनाः॥ ५४॥
ऐश्वर्यं च विशालायां पृथिव्यामपि दुर्लभम्।
पितरं मातरं चैव सम्मान्याभिप्रसाद्य च॥ ५५॥
अनुप्रव्रजितो रामं सुमित्रा येन सुप्रजाः।
आनुकूल्येन धर्मात्मा त्यक्त्वा सुखमनुत्तमम्॥ ५६॥
अनुगच्छति काकुत्स्थं भ्रातरं पालयन् वने।
सिंहस्कन्धो महाबाहुर्मनस्वी प्रियदर्शनः॥ ५७॥
पितृवद् वर्तते रामे मातृवन्मां समाचरत्।
ह्रियमाणां तदा वीरो न तु मां वेद लक्ष्मणः॥ ५८॥
वृद्धोपसेवी लक्ष्मीवान् शक्तो न बहुभाषिता।
राजपुत्रप्रियश्रेष्ठः सदृशः श्वशुरस्य मे॥ ५९॥
मत्तः प्रियतरो नित्यं भ्राता रामस्य लक्ष्मणः।
नियुक्तो धुरि यस्यां तु तामुद्वहति वीर्यवान्॥ ६०॥
यं दृष्ट्वा राघवो नैव वृत्तमार्यमनुस्मरत्।
स ममार्थाय कुशलं वक्तव्यो वचनान्मम॥ ६१॥
verses.m: Hanumān having spoken as aforesaid, Sītā too further spoke forthwith as follows: “Make on my behalf inquiries concerning the welfare of that protector of the world whom the high-minded Kausalyā brought forth, and greet Śrī Rāma with your head bent low. Inquiries concerning welfare should be addressed on my behalf and in my name to Lakṣmaṇa, that heroic and powerful younger brother of Śrī Rāma, who, having renounced garlands and all kinds of jewels as well as women, who were agreeable and excellent, nay, a dominion which was hard to attain on this vast globe, and even in heaven, as also unsurpassed felicity, and having offered profound respects to and pacified his father and mother, followed Śrī Rāma in the latter’s exile, nay, because of whom Sumitrā has earned the title of a blessed mother, nay, whose mind is given to piety, who follows his eldest brother, Śrī Rāma (a scion of Kakutstha) with devotion in the forest watching over him as a bodyguard, who has shoulders broad like those of a lion, is mighty-armed, steady-minded, and pleasing to look upon, who behaves towards Śrī Rāma as towards his father and treated me as his own mother, who did not know at all of my being borne away at the time of the occurrence, who serves his elders, is glorious and energetic, yet measured in speech, who is the foremost of those beloved of that prince, Śrī Rāma, and a replica in gallantry of my father-in-law, King Daśaratha, who is ever dearer to Śrī Rāma more than I and who willingly and efficiently shoulders the responsibility with which he is saddled and on seeing whom Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, ceases to remember his deceased father. (53—61)

verses.text:
मृदुर्नित्यं शुचिर्दक्षः प्रियो रामस्य लक्ष्मणः।
यथा हि वानरश्रेष्ठ दुःखक्षयकरो भवेत्॥ ६२॥
verses.m: “Nay, the inquiry should be addressed to him in such a way that Lakṣmaṇa, an ever mild, pure and clever darling of Śrī Rāma, O jewel among monkeys, may bring my woes to an end. (62)

verses.text:
त्वमस्मिन् कार्यनिर्वाहे प्रमाणं हरियूथप।
राघवस्त्वत्समारम्भान्मयि यत्नपरो भवेत्॥ ६३॥
verses.m: “You are upto the accomplishment of this task, O leader of monkey hordes ! By your effort alone can Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, be active on my behalf. (63)

verses.text:
इदं ब्रूयाश्च मे नाथं शूरं रामं पुनः पुनः।
जीवितं धारयिष्यामि मासं दशरथात्मज॥ ६४॥
verses.m: “Also please submit again and again to my lord, the valiant Śrī Rāma, as follows : ‘I am going to survive only a month, O son of Daśaratha ! (64)

verses.text:
ऊर्ध्वं मासान्न जीवेयं सत्येनाहं ब्रवीमि ते।
रावणेनोपरुद्धां मां निकृत्या पापकर्मणा।
त्रातुमर्हसि वीर त्वं पातालादिव कौशिकीम्॥ ६५॥
verses.m: “ ‘Out of time-limit set for my survival, only one month is left now. I shall thus not live beyond a month. I swear to you by truth. You ought to rescue me, confined as I am by Rāvaṇa of sinful deeds and subjected to persecution at the hands of ogresses, O heroic prince, even as Lord Viṣṇu in His descent as the Divine Boar rescued Goddess Earth, born in the line of Sage Kauśika from Pātāla (the nethermost subterranean region).’ ” (65)

verses.text:
ततो वस्त्रगतं मुक्त्वा दिव्यं चूडामणिं शुभम्।
प्रदेयो राघवायेति सीता हनुमते ददौ॥ ६६॥
verses.m: Untying the bright divine jewel for her head, tied in her garment, Sītā thereupon gave it to Hanumān, saying that it be delivered to Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu). (66)

verses.text:
प्रतिगृह्य ततो वीरो मणिरत्नमनुत्तमम्।
अङ्गुल्या योजयामास नह्यस्य प्राभवद् भुजः॥ ६७॥
verses.m: Taking from Sītā’s hand the excellent jewel, which was invaluable, the hero Hanumān placed it on his finger since his arm (even though he had resumed his former tiny form) was too thick for it. (67)

verses.text:
मणिरत्नं कपिवरः प्रतिगृह्याभिवाद्य च।
सीतां प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा प्रणतः पार्श्वतः स्थितः॥ ६८॥
verses.m: Taking and greeting the excellent jewel and walking round Sītā clockwise as a mark of respect, Hanumān, the foremost of monkeys, stood bent low by her side. (68)

verses.text:
हर्षेण महता युक्तः सीतादर्शनजेन सः।
हृदयेन गतो रामं लक्ष्मणं च सलक्षणम्॥ ६९॥
verses.m: Filled with great delight born of Sītā’s discovery, he mentally sought the presence of Śrī Rāma, who was endowed with auspicious bodily marks, and Lakṣmaṇa.(69)

verses.text:
मणिवरमुपगृह्य तं महार्हं
जनकनृपात्मजया धृतं प्रभावात्।
गिरिवरपवनावधूतमुक्तः
सुखितमनाः प्रतिसंक्रमं प्रपेदे॥ ७०॥
verses.m: Rejoiced at heart to receive that valuable and superb jewel, borne on her person by the daughter of King Janaka by dint of her asceticism (so that it remained unnoticed by the ogresses all the while). His conditioned resembled the one fully accomplished and happy, who was once shaken by a blast coming from the top of a huge mountain and then delivered from it, Hanumān prepared to set out on his return journey. (70)

verses.text:
मणिं दत्त्वा ततः सीता हनूमन्तमथाब्रवीत्।
अभिज्ञानमभिज्ञातमेतद् रामस्य तत्त्वतः॥ १॥
verses.m: Having parted with her jewel, Sītā then spoke to Hanumān forthwith as follows: “This token is fully known to Śrī Rāma in its reality. (1)

verses.text:
मणिं दृष्ट्वा तु रामो वै त्रयाणां संस्मरिष्यति।
वीरो जनन्या मम च राज्ञो दशरथस्य च॥ २॥
verses.m: “Seeing the jewel, the heroic Śrī Rāma for his part will surely call to mind three individuals all at once, viz., my mother, King Daśaratha and myself as it was given as a dowry to me by my mother in the presence of my father-in-law. (2)

verses.text:
स भूयस्त्वं समुत्साहचोदितो हरिसत्तम।
अस्मिन् कार्यसमुत्साहे प्रचिन्तय यदुत्तरम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Goaded further by extraordinary zeal, O jewel among monkeys, consider carefully what is to be done next for giving impetus to this work of rescuing me. (3)

verses.text:
त्वमस्मिन् कार्यनिर्योगे प्रमाणं हरिसत्तम।
तस्य चिन्तय यो यत्नो दुःखक्षयकरो भवेत्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “You alone are capable of bringing this task to completion, O jewel among monkeys ! Please consider what effort might bring my misfortunes to an end. (4)

verses.text:
हनूमन् यत्नमास्थाय दुःखक्षयकरो भव।
स तथेति प्रतिज्ञाय मारुतिर्भीमविक्रमः॥ ५॥
शिरसाऽऽवन्द्य वैदेहीं गमनायोपचक्रमे।
ज्ञात्वा सम्प्रस्थितं देवी वानरं पवनात्मजम्॥ ६॥
बाष्पगद्गदया वाचा मैथिली वाक्यमब्रवीत्।
हनूमन् कुशलं ब्रूयाः सहितौ रामलक्ष्मणौ॥ ७॥
सुग्रीवं च सहामात्यं सर्वान् वृद्धांश्च वानरान्।
ब्रूयास्त्वं वानरश्रेष्ठ कुशलं धर्मसंहितम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Remaining active, therefore, O Hanumān, pray, terminate my suffering.” Giving his assurance in the words “Be it so”, and making obeisance to Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory, with his head bent low, Hanumān, son of the wind-god, of redoubtable prowess made ready to depart. Perceiving Hanumān, sprung from the loins of the wind-god, fully prepared to leave, Sītā, a princess of Mithila, spoke as follows in a voice choked with tears: “Communicate my welfare to Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa together, O Hanumān ! Nay, make a report in consonance with righteousness regarding my welfare, O jewel among monkeys, to Sugrīva and his ministers, as also to all elderly monkeys. (5—8)

verses.text:
यथा च स महाबाहुर्मां तारयति राघवः।
अस्माद् दुःखाम्बुसंरोधात् त्वं समाधातुमर्हसि॥ ९॥
verses.m: “You ought to make efforts to see that the mighty-armed scion of Raghu delivers me from this ocean of sorrow. (9)

verses.text:
जीवन्तीं मां यथा रामः सम्भावयति कीर्तिमान्।
तत् त्वया हनुमन् वाच्यं वाचा धर्ममवाप्नुहि॥ १०॥
verses.m: “My case should be put by you in such a way, O Hanumān, that the illustrious Śrī Rāma may find me alive. Reap the virtue of rendering help to me by your words. (10)

verses.text:
नित्यमुत्साहयुक्तस्य वाचः श्रुत्वा मयेरिताः।
वर्धिष्यते दाशरथेः पौरुषं मदवाप्तये॥ ११॥
verses.m: “The effort of Śrī Rāma (son of Daśaratha), who is ever full of determination to recover me, will be intensified on hearing the words uttered by me. (11)

verses.text:
मत्संदेशयुता वाचस्त्वत्तः श्रुत्वैव राघवः।
पराक्रमे मतिं वीरो विधिवत् संविधास्यति॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Only after hearing from you the words conveying my message, the heroic Śrī Rāma will duly set his heart on exhibiting his valour.” (12)

verses.text:
सीतायास्तद् वचः श्रुत्वा हनूमान् मारुतात्मजः।
शिरस्यञ्जलिमाधाय वाक्यमुत्तरमब्रवीत्॥ १३॥
verses.m: Placing his joined palms above his head on hearing the aforesaid appeal of Sītā, Hanumān, sprung from the loins of the wind-god, made the following reply: (13)

verses.text:
क्षिप्रमेष्यति काकुत्स्थो हर्यृक्षप्रवरैर्वृतः।
यस्ते युधि विजित्यारीन् शोकं व्यपनयिष्यति॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Surrounded by the foremost of monkeys and bears, Śrī Rāma (a scion of Kakutstha), who, having conquered his enemies on the field of battle, will completely drive away your grief, will soon make his appearance here. (14)

verses.text:
नहि पश्यामि मर्त्येषु नासुरेषु सुरेषु वा।
यस्तस्य वमतो बाणान् स्थातुमुत्सहतेऽग्रतः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “I know of none among mortals, demons or gods, who would dare stand before him while he is shooting arrows. (15)

verses.text:
अप्यर्कमपि पर्जन्यमपि वैवस्वतं यमम्।
स हि सोढुं रणे शक्तस्तव हेतोर्विशेषतः॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Indeed he would be able to withstand in combat even the sun-god, Indra (the rain-god), Yama (the god of retribution), son of the sun-god, particularly for your sake. (16)

verses.text:
स हि सागरपर्यन्तां महीं साधितुमर्हति।
त्वन्निमित्तो हि रामस्य जयो जनकनन्दिनि॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Śrī Rāma can conquer the earth bounded by the ocean. Hence Śrī Rāma’s victory in your cause is certain, O daughter of Janaka !” (17)

verses.text:
तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा सम्यक् सत्यं सुभाषितम्।
जानकी बहु मेने तं वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्॥ १८॥
verses.m: Hearing the aforesaid reply of Hanumān, which was reasonable, truthful and beautifully worded, the daughter of Janaka held him in great estimation and proceeded to speak as follows : (18)

verses.text:
ततस्तं प्रस्थितं सीता वीक्षमाणा पुनः पुनः।
भर्तृस्नेहान्वितं वाक्यं सौहार्दादनुमानयत्॥ १९॥
verses.m: Gazing again and again on Hanumān, who had then made ready to depart, Sītā uttered the following respectful words, expressive of her husband’s affection for her, actuated as she was with goodwill for him: (19)

verses.text:
यदि वा मन्यसे वीर वसैकाहमरिंदम।
कस्मिंश्चित् संवृते देशे विश्रान्तः श्वो गमिष्यसि॥ २०॥
verses.m: “If you deem fit, O hero, halt for a day, O tamer of foes! Resting in some covered place, you may leave tomorrow. (20)

verses.text:
मम चैवाल्पभाग्यायाः सांनिध्यात् तव वानर।
अस्य शोकस्य महतो मुहूर्तं मोक्षणं भवेत्॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Due to your presence, O Hanumān, I shall be rid for a while, unfortunate as I am, of this violent grief. (21)

verses.text:
ततो हि हरिशार्दूल पुनरागमनाय तु।
प्राणानामपि संदेहो मम स्यान्नात्र संशयः॥ २२॥
verses.m: “For, if after that there is any doubt about your return, O tiger among monkeys, there is uncertainty of my survival too: there is no doubt about it. (22)

verses.text:
तवादर्शनजः शोको भूयो मां परितापयेत्।
दुःखादुःखपरामृष्टां दीपयन्निव वानर॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Grief born of your absence, O monkey, will torment me further, burning me, as it were, seized as I already am with agony after agony. (23)

verses.text:
अयं च वीर संदेहस्तिष्ठतीव ममाग्रतः।
सुमहांस्त्वत्सहायेषु हर्यृक्षेषु हरीश्वर॥ २४॥
कथं नु खलु दुष्पारं तरिष्यन्ति महोदधिम्।
तानि हर्यृक्षसैन्यानि तौ वा नरवरात्मजौ॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Nay, this very great doubt ever stands before me as it were about your associate monkeys and bears, O heroic lord of monkeys, as to how on earth those hordes of monkeys and bears, or, for that matter, those two princes will actually be able to cross the vast sea, which is so difficult to cross. (24-25)

verses.text:
त्रयाणामेव भूतानां सागरस्येह लङ्घने।
शक्तिः स्याद् वैनतेयस्य तव वा मारुतस्य वा॥ २६॥
verses.m: “The capacity to cross the sea in this world exists in three created beings only, viz., Garuḍa (son of Vinatā), the wind-god and yourself. (26)

verses.text:
तदस्मिन् कार्यनिर्योगे वीरैवं दुरतिक्रमे।
किं पश्यसे समाधानं त्वं हि कार्यविदां वरः॥ २७॥
verses.m: “What means do you perceive, O hero, for the accomplishment of this task, which is so very hard to get through? For, you are the foremost of those who know how to accomplish a task. (27)

verses.text:
काममस्य त्वमेवैकः कार्यस्य परिसाधने।
पर्याप्तः परवीरघ्न यशस्यस्ते फलोदयः॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Although you are definitely equal to the accomplishment of this task of rescuing me single-handed, O destroyer of hostile warriors, the attainment of success in that case will redound to your own glory rather than to that of Śrī Rāma. (28)

verses.text:
बलैः समग्रैर्युधि मां रावणं जित्य संयुगे।
विजयी स्वपुरं यायात् तत्तस्य सदृशं भवेत्॥ २९॥
verses.m: “If, on the other hand, conquering Rāvaṇa on the battlefield with the help of all his forces, Śrī Rāma returns victorious in combat to his own capital, that indeed would be worthy of him. (29)

verses.text:
बलैस्तु संकुलां कृत्वा लङ्कां परबलार्दनः।
मां नयेद् यदि काकुत्स्थस्तत् तस्य सदृशं भवेत्॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “If, overrunning Laṅkā with his forces, Śrī Rāma (a scion of Kakutstha) the scourge of hostile forces, for his part, takes me back from Laṅkā, that alone would be worthy of him. (30)

verses.text:
तद्यथा तस्य विक्रान्तमनुरूपं महात्मनः।
भवेदाहवशूरस्य तथा त्वमुपपादय॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Therefore, act you in such a way that the exalted soul, valiant in combat, may exhibit prowess worthy of him.” (31)

verses.text:
तदर्थोपहितं वाक्यं प्रश्रितं हेतुसंहितम्।
निशम्य हनुमान् शेषं वाक्यमुत्तरमब्रवीत्॥ ३२॥
verses.m: Hearing the aforesaid utterance of Sītā, which was full of significance, polite and logical, Hanumān made the following final reply: (32)

verses.text:
देवि हर्यृक्षसैन्यानामीश्वरः प्लवतां वरः।
सुग्रीवः सत्यसम्पन्नस्तवार्थे कृतनिश्चयः॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “The lord of the monkey and bear hordes and the foremost of monkeys, Sugrīva, who is richly endowed with truthfulness, is determined to liberate you, O godlike lady ! (33)

verses.text:
स वानरसहस्राणां कोटीभिरभिसंवृतः।
क्षिप्रमेष्यति वैदेहि राक्षसानां निबर्हणः॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “Surrounded by crores of monkeys, O princess of the Videha territory, that destroyer of ogres will make his appearance soon. (34)

verses.text:
तस्य विक्रमसम्पन्नाः सत्त्ववन्तो महाबलाः।
मनःसंकल्पसम्पाता निदेशे हरयः स्थिताः॥ ३५॥
येषां नोपरि नाधस्तान्न तिर्यक् सज्जते गतिः।
न च कर्मसु सीदन्ति महत्स्वमिततेजसः॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “Monkeys, who are richly endowed with valour, full of courage and extraordinarily mighty, nay, who can leap to any distance according to their mental resolve, whose course is impeded neither upwards nor downwards nor to their right or left, who never lose heart even in great undertakings and are endowed with extraordinary energy, remain standing at Sugrīva’s beck and call. (35-36)

verses.text:
असकृत् तैर्महोत्साहैः ससागरधराधरा।
प्रदक्षिणीकृता भूमिर्वायुमार्गानुसारिभिः॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “The earth including the oceans and mountains has been circumambulated by them clockwise more than once following the aerial path, endowed as they are with extraordinary energy. (37)

verses.text:
मद्विशिष्टाश्च तुल्याश्च सन्ति तत्र वनौकसः।
मत्तः प्रत्यवरः कश्चिन्नास्ति सुग्रीवसंनिधौ॥ ३८॥
verses.m: “There exist in that army monkeys who are my equals and even superior to me. None is inferior to me in the company of Sugrīva. (38)

verses.text:
अहं तावदिह प्राप्तः किं पुनस्ते महाबलाः।
नहि प्रकृष्टाः प्रेष्यन्ते प्रेष्यन्ते हीतरे जनाः॥ ३९॥
verses.m: “When I have arrived here, how easily can they arrive, who are endowed with extraordinary might ! Surely these superior ones are not sent on errands, only the inferior ones are so sent. (39)

verses.text:
तदलं परितापेन देवि शोको व्यपैतु ते।
एकोत्पातेन ते लङ्कामेष्यन्ति हरियूथपाः॥ ४०॥
verses.m: “Therefore, have done with sorrowing, O godlike lady ! Let your grief disappear. In a single bound those leaders of monkey hordes will reach Laṅkā. (40)

verses.text:
मम पृष्ठगतौ तौ च चन्द्रसूर्याविवोदितौ।
त्वत्सकाशं महासङ्घौ नृसिंहावागमिष्यतः॥ ४१॥
verses.m: “Nay, like the sun and the moon appearing on the horizon, those two lions among men, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, followed by large multitudes, will arrive in your presence mounted on my back. (41)

verses.text:
तौ हि वीरौ नरवरौ सहितौ रामलक्ष्मणौ।
आगम्य नगरीं लङ्कां सायकैर्विधमिष्यतः॥ ४२॥
verses.m: “Arriving together, those two heroic jewels among men will undoubtedly blow away Laṅkā with their shafts. (42)

verses.text:
सगणं रावणं हत्वा राघवो रघुनन्दनः।
त्वामादाय वरारोहे स्वपुरीं प्रति यास्यति॥ ४३॥
verses.m: “Making short work of Rāvaṇa alongwith his hordes, Śrī Rāma, the delight of the Raghus, will return to his own city Ayodhyā, taking you with him, O lady of excellent limbs ! (43)

verses.text:
तदाश्वसिहि भद्रं ते भव त्वं कालकाङ्क्षिणी।
नचिराद् द्रक्ष्यसे रामं प्रज्वलन्तमिवानलम्॥ ४४॥
verses.m: “Therefore, take heart and bide you your time. May good betide you ! Before long you shall be able to see Śrī Rāma shining bright like fire. (44)

verses.text:
निहते राक्षसेन्द्रे च सपुत्रामात्यबान्धवे।
त्वं समेष्यसि रामेण शशाङ्केनेव रोहिणी॥ ४५॥
verses.m: “Nay, when Rāvaṇa, the lord of ogres, is slain with his sons, ministers and kinsfolk, you shall be re-united with Śrī Rāma as Rohiṇī (a consort of the moon god presiding over a constellation of the same name) is with the moon-god. (45)

verses.text:
क्षिप्रं त्वं देवि शोकस्य पारं द्रक्ष्यसि मैथिलि।
रावणं चैव रामेण द्रक्ष्यसे निहतं बलात्॥ ४६॥
verses.m: “Soon you shall see the end of your grief, O godlike princess of Mithilā ! Nay, you will also see Rāvaṇa killed by Śrī Rāma by force of superior might.” (46)

verses.text:
एवमाश्वास्य वैदेहीं हनूमान् मारुतात्मजः।
गमनाय मतिं कृत्वा वैदेहीं पुनरब्रवीत्॥ ४७॥
verses.m: Having comforted Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory, as above, and making up his mind to depart, Hanumān, sprung from the loins of the wind-god, spoke to Sītā once more as follows : (47)

verses.text:
तमरिघ्नं कृतात्मानं क्षिप्रं द्रक्ष्यसि राघवम्।
लक्ष्मणं च धनुष्पाणिं लङ्काद्वारमुपागतम्॥ ४८॥
verses.m: “You shall soon behold the celebrated Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu), the destroyer of his foes, who has subdued his soul, as also Lakṣmaṇa, arrived at the gate of Laṅkā, bow in hand. (48)

verses.text:
नखदंष्ट्रायुधान् वीरान् सिंहशार्दूलविक्रमान्।
वानरान् वारणेन्द्राभान् क्षिप्रं द्रक्ष्यसि संगतान्॥ ४९॥
verses.m: “At no distant date you shall also see gathered together valiant monkeys endowed with the prowess of lions and tigers, nay looking like lordly elephants and using their nails and teeth as weapons. (49)

verses.text:
शैलाम्बुदनिकाशानां लङ्कामलयसानुषु।
नर्दतां कपिमुख्यानामार्ये यूथान्यनेकशः॥ ५०॥
verses.m: “You shall see, O noble lady, numerous companies of the foremost of monkeys, looking like mountains or clouds and thundering on the peaks of the Malaya mountain in Laṅkā. (50)

verses.text:
स तु मर्मणि घोरेण ताडितो मन्मथेषुणा।
न शर्म लभते रामः सिंहार्दित इव द्विपः॥ ५१॥
verses.m: “Hit in his vulnerable parts by the formidable darts of Love, the aforesaid Śrī Rāma for his part knows no more rest than an elephant hurt by a lion. (51)

verses.text:
रुद मा देवि शोकेन मा भूत् ते मनसो भयम्।
शचीव भर्त्रा शक्रेण सङ्गमेष्यसि शोभने॥ ५२॥
verses.m: “Weep no more, O godlike lady ! Let there be no fear from grief to your mind. You shall be re-united with your husband in the same way as Śaci, the consort of Indra, was with Indra, O charming lady ! (52)

verses.text:
रामाद् विशिष्टः कोऽन्योऽस्ति कश्चित् सौमित्रिणा समः।
अग्निमारुतकल्पौ तौ भ्रातरौ तव संश्रयौ॥ ५३॥
verses.m: “Who else is superior to Śrī Rāma and who is a match for Lakṣmaṇa, son of Sumitrā? Those two brothers, who resemble fire and the wind, are your support. (53)

verses.text:
नास्मिंश्चिरं वत्स्यसि देवि देशे
रक्षोगणैरध्युषितेऽतिरौद्रे।
न ते चिरादागमनं प्रियस्य
क्षमस्व मत्संगमकालमात्रम्॥ ५४॥
verses.m: “You shall not stay long in this most fearful land inhabited by ogres, O godlike lady ! The advent of your darling will not take long. Pray, have patience only till the moment of my meeting with Śrī Rāma.”(54)

verses.text:
श्रुत्वा तु वचनं तस्य वायुसूनोर्महात्मनः।
उवाचात्महितं वाक्यं सीता सुरसुतोपमा॥ १॥
verses.m: Hearing the assurance of that high-souled son of the wind-god, Sītā, who resembled the daughter of a god, made for her part, the following reply, which was calculated to advance her own interests : (1)

verses.text:
त्वां दृष्ट्वा प्रियवक्तारं सम्प्रहृष्यामि वानर।
अर्धसंजातसस्येव वृष्टिं प्राप्य वसुंधरा॥ २॥
verses.m: “I feel thrilled to see you speaking kind words, O Hanumān, even as the earth with its crops half ripe is enlivened on having a shower. (2)

verses.text:
यथा तं पुरुषव्याघ्रं गात्रैः शोकाभिकर्शितैः।
संस्पृशेयं सकामाहं तथा कुरु दयां मयि॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Show compassion to me by manipulating things in such a way that, full of longing, I may be able to embrace that tiger among men with my limbs utterly emaciated through grief. (3)

verses.text:
अभिज्ञानं च रामस्य दद्या हरिगणोत्तम।
क्षिप्तामिषीकां काकस्य कोपादेकाक्षिशातनीम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Again, remind Śrī Rāma, O jewel among hordes of monkeys, as a token of your having met me, of the reed hurled by him in anger, which destroyed one eye of the son of Indra, who came disguised as a crow. (4)

verses.text:
मनःशिलायास्तिलको गण्डपार्श्वे निवेशितः।
त्वया प्रणष्टे तिलके तं किल स्मर्तुमर्हसि॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Further say to him, ‘You ought surely to recall the decoration which was painted by you on my (Sītā’s) cheek with realgar when my former decoration had got effaced. (5)

verses.text:
स वीर्यवान् कथं सीतां हृतां समनुमन्यसे।
वसन्तीं रक्षसां मध्ये महेन्द्रवरुणोपम॥ ६॥
verses.m: “ ‘Though powerful, how do you wink at Sītā (myself) having been borne away and living in the midst of ogres, O lord vying with Indra, the ruler of gods, and Varuṇa, the god of waters? (6)

verses.text:
एष चूडामणिर्दिव्यो मया सुपरिरक्षितः।
एतं दृष्ट्वा प्रहृष्यामि व्यसने त्वामिवानघ॥ ७॥
verses.m: “ ‘This celestial jewel for the head was preserved by me with special care, I used to feel overjoyed in adversity to see it as I did on seeing you, O sinless one ! (7)

verses.text:
एष निर्यातितः श्रीमान् मया ते वारिसम्भवः।
अतः परं न शक्ष्यामि जीवितुं शोकलालसा॥ ८॥
verses.m: “ ‘This splendid jewel, having its origin in sea-water, has been sent by me to you (Śrī Rāma). Absorbed in grief that I am, I shall no longer be able to survive beyond a month. (8)

verses.text:
असह्यानि च दुःखानि वाचश्च हृदयच्छिदः।
राक्षसैः सह संवासं त्वत्कृते मर्षयाम्यहम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “ ‘Only for your sake have I endured so long unbearable woes, words which pierced my heart and living surrounded by ogresses. (9)

verses.text:
धारयिष्यामि मासं तु जीवितं शत्रुसूदन।
मासादूर्ध्वं न जीविष्ये त्वया हीना नृपात्मज॥ १०॥
verses.m: “ ‘Anyhow I shall continue to live for a month more, O destroyer of foes ! Beyond a month, of course, I am not going to survive in your absence, O prince ! (10)

verses.text:
घोरो राक्षसराजोऽयं दृष्टिश्च न सुखा मयि।
त्वां च श्रुत्वा विषज्जन्तं न जीवेयमपि क्षणम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “ ‘Frightful is this ruler of ogres; his attitude towards me is also not favourable. On hearing of you (Śrī Rāma) tarrying, on top of all this, I may not survive even a moment longer.’ ” (11)

verses.text:
वैदेह्या वचनं श्रुत्वा करुणं साश्रुभाषितम्।
अथाब्रवीन्महातेजा हनूमान् मारुतात्मजः॥ १२॥
verses.m: Hearing the aforesaid plaintive message of Sītā, uttered with tears in her eyes, Hanumān, sprung from the loins of the wind-god, who was endowed with extraordinary energy, forthwith submitted as follows : (12)

verses.text:
त्वच्छोकविमुखो रामो देवि सत्येन ते शपे।
रामे शोकाभिभूते तु लक्ष्मणः परितप्यते॥ १३॥
verses.m: “I swear to you by truth, O godlike lady, that Śrī Rāma has grown averse to everything else through grief caused by your absence. And Lakṣmaṇa too suffers agony due to Śrī Rāma being overwhelmed with sorrow. (13)

verses.text:
दृष्टा कथंचिद् भवती न कालः परिदेवितुम्।
इमं मुहूर्तं दुःखानामन्तं द्रक्ष्यसि भामिनि॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Somehow you have been discovered by me; hence this is not the time for grieving. From this very hour you will see the end of your woes drawing near, O noble lady ! (14)

verses.text:
तावुभौ पुरुषव्याघ्रौ राजपुत्रावनिन्दितौ।
त्वद्दर्शनकृतोत्साहौ लङ्कां भस्मीकरिष्यतः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Both the aforesaid princes, who are tigers among men and are beyond reproach and who are determined to see you, will reduce Laṅkā to ashes. (15)

verses.text:
हत्वा तु समरे रक्षो रावणं सहबान्धवैः।
राघवौ त्वां विशालाक्षि स्वां पुरीं प्रति नेष्यतः॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Nay, killing in combat the ogre Rāvaṇa, alongwith his kinsfolk, the two scions of Raghu, O large-eyed lady, will take you back to their own capital. (16)

verses.text:
यत्तु रामो विजानीयादभिज्ञानमनिन्दिते।
प्रीतिसंजननं भूयस्तस्य त्वं दातुमर्हसि॥ १७॥
verses.m: “You ought further to give me a token which Śrī Rāma alone may be able to recognize and which may cause him delight, O irreproachable lady !” (17)

verses.text:
साब्रवीद् दत्तमेवाहो मयाभिज्ञानमुत्तमम्।
एतदेव हि रामस्य दृष्ट्वा यत्नेन भूषणम्॥ १८॥
श्रद्धेयं हनुमन् वाक्यं तव वीर भविष्यति।
स तं मणिवरं गृह्य श्रीमान् प्लवगसत्तमः॥ १९॥
प्रणम्य शिरसा देवीं गमनायोपचक्रमे।
तमुत्पातकृतोत्साहमवेक्ष्य हरियूथपम्॥ २०॥
वर्धमानं महावेगमुवाच जनकात्मजा।
अश्रुपूर्णमुखी दीना बाष्पगद्गदया गिरा॥ २१॥
verses.m: She replied, “An excellent token has already been handed over to you by me, O Hanumān ! On his having carefully seen this jewel alone, your statement, O gallant Hanumān, will actually prove worthy of credence to Śrī Rāma.” Having taken that excellent jewel and made respectful obeisance to the godlike lady with his head bent low, the glorious Hanumān, the foremost of monkeys, prepared to depart. Observing that leader of monkey hordes, who was possessed of great impetuosity, expanding and striving to leap across the sea, Sītā, Janaka’s daughter, spoke as follows in a voice choked with sobs, her face bathed in tears, distressed as she was: (18—21)

verses.text:
हनूमन् सिंहसंकाशौ भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ।
सुग्रीवं च सहामात्यं सर्वान् ब्रूया अनामयम्॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Pray, apprise, O Hanumān, all, viz., the two brothers, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, who resemble a pair of lions, as well as Sugrīva and his ministers, of my welfare.(22)

verses.text:
यथा च स महाबाहुर्मां तारयति राघवः।
अस्माद् दुःखाम्बुसंरोधात् त्वं समाधातुमर्हसि॥ २३॥
verses.m: “You ought to make efforts to see that that mighty-armed scion of Raghu delivers me from this ocean of sorrow. (23)

verses.text:
इदं च तीव्रं मम शोकवेगं
रक्षोभिरेभिः परिभर्त्सनं च।
ब्रूयास्तु रामस्य गतः समीपं
शिवश्च तेऽध्वास्तु हरिप्रवीर॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Arrived in the presence of Śrī Rāma, speak to him of the acute vehemence of my grief as well as of the threats of these ogres and let your journey be happy, O great hero among the monkeys !” (24)

verses.text:
स राजपुत्र्या प्रतिवेदितार्थः
कपिः कृतार्थः परिहृष्टचेताः।
तदल्पशेषं प्रसमीक्ष्य कार्यं
दिशं ह्युदीचीं मनसा जगाम॥ २५॥
verses.m: Apprised by the princess, Sītā, of her object, nay, greatly delighted at heart on his purpose of visiting Sītā having been accomplished and thinking that only a small fraction of his duty remained to be performed, he mentally sought the northern direction. (25)

verses.text:
स च वाग्भिः प्रशस्ताभिर्गमिष्यन् पूजितस्तया।
तस्माद् देशादपाक्रम्य चिन्तयामास वानरः॥ १॥
verses.m: Moving from that place, when he had been honoured by Sītā with excellent words while he was about to depart, the aforesaid monkey, Hanumān, now thought within himself: (1)

verses.text:
अल्पशेषमिदं कार्यं दृष्टेयमसितेक्षणा।
त्रीनुपायानतिक्रम्य चतुर्थ इह दृश्यते॥ २॥
verses.m: ‘This dark-eyed lady Sītā has been seen, which was the principal object of my visit to this place. Only a small portion of my present duty still remains to be performed. Leaving out of consideration three out of the four means to success (viz., negotiation, gift and sowing seeds of dissension) the fourth, viz., punishment appears to be called for at this juncture. (2)

verses.text:
न साम रक्षःसु गुणाय कल्पते
न दानमर्थोपचितेषु युज्यते।
न भेदसाध्या बलदर्पिता जनाः
पराक्रमस्त्वेष ममेह रोचते॥ ३॥
verses.m: ‘Negotiation does not conduce to good results with ogres; gift too is not enjoined in favour of those richly endowed with wealth; people who are intoxicated with power cannot be tamed by sowing seeds of dissension in their ranks. Hence show of valour alone appeals to me on this occasion. (3)

verses.text:
न चास्य कार्यस्य पराक्रमादृते
विनिश्चयः कश्चिदिहोपपद्यते।
हतप्रवीराश्च रणे तु राक्षसाः
कथंचिदीयुर्यदिहाद्य मार्दवम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: ‘Barring show of valour no infallible means of accomplishing this task of ascertaining the strength of the ogres is practicable in these circumstances; for the ogres can adopt a meek attitude in the ensuing conflict only if their foremost heroes are somehow killed at the present moment. (4)

verses.text:
कार्ये कर्मणि निर्वृत्ते यो बहून्यपि साधयेत्।
पूर्वकार्याविरोधेन स कार्यं कर्तुमर्हति॥ ५॥
verses.m: ‘He alone can successfully accomplish his purpose, who compasses numerous secondary tasks even after the main business has been carried through, without marring the previous achievement. (5)

verses.text:
न ह्येकः साधको हेतुः स्वल्पस्यापीह कर्मणः।
यो ह्यर्थं बहुधा वेद स समर्थोऽर्थसाधने॥ ६॥
verses.m: ‘Surely there cannot be an exclusive means of accomplishing a purpose in this world, however insignificant it may be. On the other hand, he alone is capable of accomplishing a purpose, who knows to do a thing in many ways. (6)

verses.text:
इहैव तावत्कृतनिश्चयो ह्यहं
व्रजेयमद्य प्लवगेश्वरालयम्।
परात्मसम्मर्दविशेषतत्त्ववित्
ततः कृतं स्यान्मम भर्तृशासनम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: ‘If I return to the abode of Sugrīva (the lord of monkeys) today, having ascertained the truth as to who will predominate in an encounter between the enemy and ourselves, and also having determined the future course of action in this very journey, then only will the command of my master have been carried out by me in the real sense of the term. (7)

verses.text:
कथं नु खल्वद्य भवेत् सुखागतं
प्रसह्य युद्धं मम राक्षसैः सह।
तथैव खल्वात्मबलं च सारवत्
समानयेन्मां च रणे दशाननः॥ ८॥
verses.m: ‘How can my journey to this place at this juncture possibly prove to be a truly happy one? How will my encounter with the ogres come about all of a sudden? And, similarly, how indeed will that ten-headed monster Rāvaṇa actually know the strength of his own mighty troops as well as myself in a combat between us? (8)

verses.text:
ततः समासाद्य रणे दशाननं
समन्त्रिवर्गं सबलं सयायिनम्।
हृदि स्थितं तस्य मतं बलं च
सुखेन मत्वाहमितः पुनर्व्रजे॥ ९॥
verses.m: ‘Then, meeting Rāvaṇa, the ten-headed monster, his body of ministers, troops and charioteer, and conveniently reading the design enshrined in his heart, and ascertaining his strength, I shall return from this place afterwards. (9)

verses.text:
इदमस्य नृशंसस्य नन्दनोपममुत्तमम्।
वनं नेत्रमनःकान्तं नानाद्रुमलतायुतम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: ‘This excellent grove of the cruel Rāvaṇa, which vies with the Nandana grove in heaven, is pleasing to the eyes as well as to the mind and is full of trees and creepers of every variety. (10)

verses.text:
इदं विध्वंसयिष्यामि शुष्कं वनमिवानलः।
अस्मिन् भग्ने ततः कोपं करिष्यति स रावणः॥ ११॥
verses.m: ‘I shall presently lay it waste even as fire consumes a dry grove. When this has been laid waste, the notorious Rāvaṇa will forthwith give vent to his anger. (11)

verses.text:
ततो महत्साश्वमहारथद्विपं
बलं समानेष्यति राक्षसाधिपः।
त्रिशूलकालायसपट्टिशायुधं
ततो महद्युद्धमिदं भविष्यति॥ १२॥
verses.m: ‘Rāvaṇa, the suzerain lord of ogres, will thereupon lead his huge army, full of horses, large chariots and elephants and armed with tridents and spears made of iron, and a formidable struggle will then immediately follow. (12)

verses.text:
अहं च तैः संयति चण्डविक्रमैः
समेत्य रक्षोभिरभङ्गविक्रमः।
निहत्य तद् रावणचोदितं बलं
सुखं गमिष्यामि हरीश्वरालयम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: ‘Nay, coming to grips on the battle-field with those ogres of terrible prowess and destroying that army led by Rāvaṇa, my valour knowing no frustration, I shall happily return to the abode of Sugriva, the lord of monkeys.’ (13)

verses.text:
ततो मारुतवत् क्रुद्धो मारुतिर्भीमविक्रमः।
ऊरुवेगेन महता द्रुमान् क्षेप्तुमथारभत्॥ १४॥
verses.m: Furious like the wind, Hanumān (son of the wind-god) of redoubtable valour, now forthwith proceeded to fell the trees with great impetuosity of his thighs. (14)

verses.text:
ततस्तद्धनुमान् वीरो बभञ्ज प्रमदावनम्।
मत्तद्विजसमाघुष्टं नानाद्रुमलतायुतम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: The valiant Hanumān then laid waste the aforesaid pleasance attached to the gynaeceum, which was resonant with the shrieks of birds in heat and full of trees and creepers of every variety. (15)

verses.text:
तद्वनं मथितैर्वृक्षैर्भिन्नैश्च सलिलाशयैः।
चूर्णितैः पर्वताग्रैश्च बभूवाप्रियदर्शनम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: With its trees uprooted and ponds stirred up and rendered muddy and the crests of its pleasure-hills crushed, that pleasure-grove presented an unsightly appearance. (16)

verses.text:
नानाशकुन्तविरुतैः प्रभिन्नसलिलाशयैः।
ताम्रैः किसलयैः क्लान्तैः क्लान्तद्रुमलतायुतैः॥ १७॥
न बभौ तद् वनं तत्र दावानलहतं यथा।
व्याकुलावरणा रेजुर्विह्वला इव ता लताः॥ १८॥
verses.m: With the shrieks of various birds, the brinks of its ponds demolished, its coppery shoots withered, and with the myriads of its trees and creepers dried up, that pleasure-grove did not look bright on that occasion, as though it had been destroyed by a wild fire. Those creepers too with their coverings in the form of leaves displaced looked like women with their robes in disarray. (17-18)

verses.text:
लतागृहैश्चित्रगृहैश्च सादितै-
र्व्यालैर्मृगैरार्तरवैश्च पक्षिभिः।
शिलागृहैरुन्मथितैस्तथा गृहैः
प्रणष्टरूपं तदभून्महद् वनम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: With its arbours and picture-galleries destroyed, tame beasts of prey (such as tigers), deer and birds emitting cries of distress, its grottos and other structures demolished, that extensive grove presented the appearance of ruin. (19)

verses.text:
सा विह्वलाशोकलताप्रताना
वनस्थली शोकलताप्रताना।
जाता दशास्यप्रमदावनस्य
कपेर्बलाद्धि प्रमदावनस्य॥ २०॥
verses.m: Through the ferocity of the monkey, Hanumān, the woodland of that pleasure-garden, which afforded shelter to the womenfolk of Rāvaṇa (the ten-headed monster) and which was distinguished by its clusters of shaking Aśoka creepers, then became a jumble of creepers which caused grief to the lookers-on. (20)

verses.text:
ततः स कृत्वा जगतीपतेर्महान्
महद् व्यलीकं मनसो महात्मनः।
युयुत्सुरेको बहुभिर्महाबलैः
श्रिया ज्वलंस्तोरणमाश्रितः कपिः॥ २१॥
verses.m: Having perpetrated something which was utterly displeasing to the mind of the high minded ruler of the land of Laṅkā, and eager to contend single-handed with a number of warriors endowed with extraordinary might, the great monkey, Hanumān, took up his position at the entrance of the pleasance, blazing with martial glory. (21)

verses.text:
ततः पक्षिनिनादेन वृक्षभङ्गस्वनेन च।
बभूवुस्त्राससम्भ्रान्ताः सर्वे लङ्कानिवासिनः॥ १॥
verses.m: Thereupon all the denizens of Laṅkā got terror-stricken at the screaming of birds and the crash of falling trees. (1)

verses.text:
विद्रुताश्च भयत्रस्ता विनेदुर्मृगपक्षिणः।
रक्षसां च निमित्तानि क्रूराणि प्रतिपेदिरे॥ २॥
verses.m: Put to flight, being panic-stricken, beasts and birds began to scream. Nay, fierce portents made their appearance before the ogres. (2)

verses.text:
ततो गतायां निद्रायां राक्षस्यो विकृताननाः।
तद् वनं ददृशुर्भग्नं तं च वीरं महाकपिम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: Their sleep having consequently vanished, the ugly-faced ogresses found that grove devastated and saw that huge and gallant monkey before them. (3)

verses.text:
स ता दृष्ट्वा महाबाहुर्महासत्त्वो महाबलः।
चकार सुमहद्रूपं राक्षसीनां भयावहम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: Beholding them, the mighty-armed Hanumān, who was endowed with extraordinary courage and might, assumed a gigantic form striking terror into the ogresses. (4)

verses.text:
ततस्तु गिरिसंकाशमतिकायं महाबलम्।
राक्षस्यो वानरं दृष्ट्वा पप्रच्छुर्जनकात्मजाम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: Seeing a colossal monkey looking like a mountain and endowed with extraordinary strength, the ogresses for their part forthwith questioned the daughter of Janaka as follows: (5)

verses.text:
कोऽयं कस्य कुतो वायं किंनिमित्तमिहागतः।
कथं त्वया सहानेन संवादः कृत इत्युत॥ ६॥
आचक्ष्व नो विशालाक्षि मा भूत्ते सुभगे भयम्।
संवादमसितापाङ्गि त्वया किं कृतवानयम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Please tell us, O large-eyed lady, who this creature is, whose messenger is he, whence and what for he has come and also wherefore talk was held by him with you. No fear need be entertained by you, O graceful lady ! What conversation did he have with you, O lady with dark-cornered eyes?” (6-7)

verses.text:
अथाब्रवीत् तदा साध्वी सीता सर्वाङ्गशोभना।
रक्षसां कामरूपाणां विज्ञाने का गतिर्मम॥ ८॥
verses.m: The virtuous Sītā, who was charming of every limb, then replied forthwith as follows: “What means can I have for acquiring correct knowledge about the ogres, who are capable of changing their form at will? (8)

verses.text:
यूयमेवास्य जानीत योऽयं यद् वा करिष्यति।
अहिरेव ह्यहेः पादान् विजानाति न संशयः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “You alone ought to know who he is and what he is about. Indeed a serpent alone has true knowledge about the movements of a serpent: there is no doubt about it. (9)

verses.text:
अहमप्यतिभीतास्मि नैव जानामि को ह्ययम्।
वेद्मि राक्षसमेवैनं कामरूपिणमागतम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: “I too am exceedingly frightened and do not know at all who he really is. Of course, I believe him to be an ogre able to change his form at will, arrived here.” (10)

verses.text:
वैदेह्या वचनं श्रुत्वा राक्षस्यो विद्रुता द्रुतम्।
स्थिताः काश्चिद्गताः काश्चिद् रावणाय निवेदितुम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: Hearing the reply of Sītā (a princess of the Videha territory), the ogresses fled with all speed. Some of them remained rooted there, while others left to report the matter to Rāvaṇa. (11)

verses.text:
रावणस्य समीपे तु राक्षस्यो विकृताननाः।
विरूपं वानरं भीमं रावणाय न्यवेदिषुः॥ १२॥
verses.m: Arrived in the presence of Rāvaṇa, the ugly-faced ogresses for their part reported to Rāvaṇa the presence of a monstrous and redoubtable monkey in the following words: (12)

verses.text:
अशोकवनिकामध्ये राजन् भीमवपुः कपिः।
सीतया कृतसंवादस्तिष्ठत्यमितविक्रमः॥ १३॥
verses.m: “A monkey of terrible proportions and endowed with immense prowess stands, O king, in the heart of the Aśoka grove, having held a talk with Sītā. (13)

verses.text:
न च तं जानकी सीता हरिं हरिणलोचना।
अस्माभिर्बहुधा पृष्टा निवेदयितुमिच्छति॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Though questioned by us in many ways, Sītā, Janaka’s daughter, whose eyes resemble those of a doe, however, does not wish to disclose the identity of the monkey. (14)

verses.text:
वासवस्य भवेद् दूतो दूतो वैश्रवणस्य वा।
प्रेषितो वापि रामेण सीतान्वेषणकाङ्क्षया॥ १५॥
verses.m: “He may be an emissary of Indra (the ruler of gods) or an envoy of Kubera (the god of riches) or he may have been dispatched even by Rāma with intent to have Sītā traced out. (15)

verses.text:
तेनैवाद्भुतरूपेण यत्तत्तव मनोहरम्।
नानामृगगणाकीर्णं प्रमृष्टं प्रमदावनम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: “By that very monkey of marvellous form has your soul-captivating pleasance, which was crowded with herds of beasts of every variety, has been laid waste. (16)

verses.text:
न तत्र कश्चिदुद्देशो यस्तेन न विनाशितः।
यत्र सा जानकी देवी स तेन न विनाशितः॥ १७॥
verses.m: “There is not a single quarter in that pleasance, which has not been utterly devastated by him. That place alone where lives that godlike lady, Sītā, Janaka’s daughter, has not been destroyed. (17)

verses.text:
जानकीरक्षणार्थं वा श्रमाद् वा नोपलक्ष्यते।
अथवा कः श्रमस्तस्य सैव तेनाभिरक्षिता॥ १८॥
verses.m: “It is not definitely known whether he has spared it with a view to saving her or due to exhaustion. Or, since exhaustion is unknown to him, Janaka’s daughter has definitely been saved by him. (18)

verses.text:
चारुपल्लवपत्राढ्यं यं सीता स्वयमास्थिता।
प्रवृद्धः शिंशपावृक्षः स च तेनाभिरक्षितः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “That fully developed Śiṁśapā tree too, which is rich in lovely foliage and in the shade of which Sītā herself remains ensconced has been spared by him. (19)

verses.text:
तस्योग्ररूपस्योग्रं त्वं दण्डमाज्ञातुमर्हसि।
सीता सम्भाषिता येन वनं तेन विनाशितम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: “You ought to enjoin some severe punishment on that monkey having a frightful form, by whom Sītā has been spoken to. By him alone has the grove been devastated. (20)

verses.text:
मनःपरिगृहीतां तां तव रक्षोगणेश्वर।
कः सीतामभिभाषेत यो न स्यात् त्यक्तजीवितः॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Who would dare to talk with Sītā, who has been mentally accepted by you, save him who has given up all hope of survival, O ruler of ogre hordes?” (21)

verses.text:
राक्षसीनां वचः श्रुत्वा रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः।
चिताग्निरिव जज्वाल कोपसंवर्तितेक्षणः॥ २२॥
verses.m: Hearing the report of the ogresses, Rāvaṇa, the lord of ogres, flared up like a funeral fire, his eyes rolling rapidly through rage. (22)

verses.text:
तस्य क्रुद्धस्य नेत्राभ्यां प्रापतन्नश्रुबिन्दवः।
दीप्ताभ्यामिव दीपाभ्यां सार्चिषः स्नेहबिन्दवः॥ २३॥
verses.m: From his eyes, angry as he was, trickled down tear-drops like burning drops of oil from a pair of kindled lights. (23)

verses.text:
आत्मनः सदृशान् वीरान् किंकरान्नाम राक्षसान्।
व्यादिदेश महातेजा निग्रहार्थं हनूमतः॥ २४॥
verses.m: Rāvaṇa, who was endowed with extraordinary energy, ordered in particular valiant ogres, named Kiṅkaras, who vied with himself, to capture Hanumān. (24)

verses.text:
तेषामशीतिसाहस्रं किंकराणां तरस्विनाम्।
निर्ययुर्भवनात् तस्मात् कूटमुद्गरपाणयः॥ २५॥
verses.m: Of the aforesaid energetic Kiṅkaras, eighty thousand sallied forth from that palace, iron mallets and clubs in hand. (25)

verses.text:
महोदरा महादंष्ट्रा घोररूपा महाबलाः।
युद्धाभिमनसः सर्वे हनूमद्ग्रहणोन्मुखाः॥ २६॥
verses.m: They were all big-bellied, had large teeth and of terrible form, were endowed with extraordinary might, inclined to fighting and eager to lay hold on Hanumān. (26)

verses.text:
ते कपिं तं समासाद्य तोरणस्थमवस्थितम्।
अभिपेतुर्महावेगाः पतंगा इव पावकम्॥ २७॥
verses.m: Duly approaching the aforesaid monkey, who was stationed at the archway, ready to fight, they darted at him with great vehemence like moths rushing towards a flame. (27)

verses.text:
ते गदाभिर्विचित्राभिः परिघैः काञ्चनाङ्गदैः।
आजग्मुर्वानरश्रेष्ठं शरैरादित्यसंनिभैः॥ २८॥
verses.m: They assailed Hanumān, the foremost of monkeys, with maces of different kinds, iron bludgeons plated with gold at the head and arrows shining brightly as the sun. (28)

verses.text:
मुद्गरैः पट्टिशैः शूलैः प्रासतोमरपाणयः।
परिवार्य हनूमन्तं सहसा तस्थुरग्रतः॥ २९॥
verses.m: Surrounding Hanumān, the Kiṅkaras, who were equipped with clubs, sharp-edged spears and iron pikes and who carried lances and javelins in their hands, stood all of a sudden in front of him. (29)

verses.text:
हनूमानपि तेजस्वी श्रीमान् पर्वतसंनिभः।
क्षितावाविद्ध्य लाङ्गूलं ननाद च महाध्वनिम्॥ ३०॥
verses.m: Lashing his tail at the ground, the glorious Hanumān too, who was full of energy and looked like a mountain, uttered a loud roar. (30)

verses.text:
स भूत्वा तु महाकायो हनूमान् मारुतात्मजः।
पुच्छमास्फोटयामास लङ्कां शब्देन पूरयन्॥ ३१॥
verses.m: Assuming a gigantic form, the celebrated Hanumān, sprung from the loins of the wind-god, waved his tail to and fro, filling Laṅkā with its sound. (31)

verses.text:
तस्यास्फोटितशब्देन महता चानुनादिना।
पेतुर्विहङ्गा गगनादुच्चैश्चेदमघोषयत्॥ ३२॥
verses.m: At the loud and resonant sound of the swishing of his tail, birds fell from the airspace and he proclaimed in aloud voice: (32)

verses.text:
जयत्यतिबलो रामो लक्ष्मणश्च महाबलः।
राजा जयति सुग्रीवो राघवेणाभिपालितः॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “Victorious is Śrī Rāma, who is possessed of surpassing strength and Lakṣmaṇa, who is endowed with extraordinary might. Victorious too is King Sugrīva, protected on all sides by Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu. (33)

verses.text:
दासोऽहं कोसलेन्द्रस्य रामस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः।
हनूमान् शत्रुसैन्यानां निहन्ता मारुतात्मजः॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “I, Hanumān, sprung from the loins of the wind-god, and the destroyer of hostile armies, am a servant of Śrī Rāma of unwearied action, the lord of Kośala. (34)

verses.text:
न रावणसहस्रं मे युद्धे प्रतिबलं भवेत्।
शिलाभिश्च प्रहरतः पादपैश्च सहस्रशः॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “Not even a thousand of Rāvaṇas can stand my might in combat, even as I assail them with a myriad of rocks and trees. (35)

verses.text:
अर्दयित्वा पुरीं लङ्कामभिवाद्य च मैथिलीम्।
समृद्धार्थो गमिष्यामि मिषतां सर्वरक्षसाम्॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “Destroying the city of Laṅkā and greeting Sītā, the princess of Mithilā, I shall return fully accomplished of purpose, while all the ogres stand looking on.” (36)

verses.text:
तस्य संनादशब्देन तेऽभवन् भयशङ्किताः।
ददृशुश्च हनूमन्तं संध्यामेघमिवोन्नतम्॥ ३७॥
verses.m: The Kiṅkaras were stricken with fear at his roar and beheld Hanumān standing aloft as an evening cloud. (37)

verses.text:
स्वामिसंदेशनिःशङ्कास्ततस्ते राक्षसाः कपिम्।
चित्रैः प्रहरणैर्भीमैरभिपेतुस्ततस्ततः॥ ३८॥
verses.m: Rid of all doubt as to who he was by the mention of his master, those ogres thereupon attacked him from every side with various dreadful weapons. (38)

verses.text:
स तैः परिवृतः शूरैः सर्वतः स महाबलः।
आससादायसं भीमं परिघं तोरणाश्रितम्॥ ३९॥
verses.m: Surrounded by those valiant ogres from all sides, the celebrated Hanumān, who was endowed with extraordinary might, seized a formidable iron bar lying at the archway. (39)

verses.text:
स तं परिघमादाय जघान रजनीचरान्।
सपन्नगमिवादाय स्फुरन्तं विनतासुतः॥ ४०॥
verses.m: Laying hold on that bar, he struck the rangers of the night even as Garuḍa (son of Vinatā) would, carrying a struggling serpent. (40)

verses.text:
विचचाराम्बरे वीरः परिगृह्य च मारुतिः।
सूदयामास वज्रेण दैत्यानिव सहस्रदृक्॥ ४१॥
verses.m: Nay, grasping the bar tightly, the gallant Hanumān, son of the wind-god, ranged through the air and began to destroy the ogres even as Indra (the god with a thousand eyes) killed the Daityas (sons of Diti) with his thunderbolt. (41)

verses.text:
स हत्वा राक्षसान् वीरः किंकरान् मारुतात्मजः।
युद्धाकाङ्क्षी महावीरस्तोरणं समवस्थितः॥ ४२॥
verses.m: Having made short work of the ogres known by the collective name of Kiṅkaras, the aforesaid valiant Hanumān, who was an eminent hero, stood rooted at the gate thirsting for combat. (42)

verses.text:
ततस्तस्माद् भयान्मुक्ताः कतिचित्तत्र राक्षसाः।
निहतान् किंकरान् सर्वान् रावणाय न्यवेदयन्॥ ४३॥
verses.m: Free from that fear, being at a considerable distance from Hanumān, a few ogres, who had survived there, spoke to Rāvaṇa of all the Kiṅkaras having been disposed of. (43)

verses.text:
स राक्षसानां निहतं महाबलं
निशम्य राजा परिवृत्तलोचनः।
समादिदेशाप्रतिमं पराक्रमे
प्रहस्तपुत्रं समरे सुदुर्जयम्॥ ४४॥
verses.m: Hearing of the large army of ogres having been wiped out, King Rāvaṇa whose eyes began to roll rapidly through rage, duly commanded Jambumālī, son of Prahasta, who was unequalled in prowess and was most difficult to conquer in battle. (44)

verses.text:
ततः स किंकरान् हत्वा हनूमान् ध्यानमास्थितः।
वनं भग्नं मया चैत्यप्रासादो न विनाशितः॥ १॥
verses.m: Having killed the Kiṅkaras, the celebrated Hanumān then thought to himself : ‘The grove has been devastated by me, but the edifice of the sanctuary, sacred to the guardian deity of the ogres, has not been demolished.’ (1)

verses.text:
तस्मात् प्रासादमद्यैवमिमं विध्वंसयाम्यहम्।
इति संचिन्त्य हनुमान् मनसादर्शयन् बलम्॥ २॥
verses.m: Hanumān, therefore, stood revolving in his mind as follows : ‘Exhibiting my strength, I shall, therefore, likewise destroy this edifice today.’ (2)

verses.text:
चैत्यप्रासादमुत्प्लुत्य मेरुशृङ्गमिवोन्नतम्।
आरुरोह हरिश्रेष्ठो हनूमान् मारुतात्मजः॥ ३॥
verses.m: Taking a leap, Hanumān, the foremost of monkeys, climbed up the edifice of the sanctuary, which was high as a peak of Mount Meru. (3)

verses.text:
आरुह्य गिरिसंकाशं प्रासादं हरियूथपः।
बभौ स सुमहातेजाः प्रतिसूर्य इवोदितः॥ ४॥
verses.m: Climbing up the edifice, which closely resembled a mountain, that leader of monkey hordes, Hanumān, who was endowed with extraordinary effulgence, looked like a second sun, just risen. (4)

verses.text:
सम्प्रधृष्य तु दुर्धर्षश्चैत्यप्रासादमुन्नतम्।
हनूमान् प्रज्वलँल्लक्ष्म्या पारियात्रोपमोऽभवत्॥ ५॥
verses.m: Blazing with glory on having assailed that lofty edifice of the sanctuary, Hanumān for his part, who was difficult to challenge, shone like the Pāriyātra mountain (one of the seven principal mountains of India). (5)

verses.text:
स भूत्वा सुमहाकायः प्रभावान् मारुतात्मजः।
धृष्टमास्फोटयामास लङ्कां शब्देन पूरयन्॥ ६॥
verses.m: Assuming immense proportions by dint of his glory, Hanumān, sprung from the loins of the wind-god, boldly began to demolish the sanctuary filling Laṅkā with the crash. (6)

verses.text:
तस्यास्फोटितशब्देन महता श्रोत्रघातिना।
पेतुर्विहंगमास्तत्र चैत्यपालाश्च मोहिताः॥ ७॥
verses.m: At the loud and deafening sound of his act of demolition, the birds as well as the guards of the sanctuary toppled down senseless on the spot. (7)

verses.text:
अस्त्रविज्जयतां रामो लक्ष्मणश्च महाबलः।
राजा जयति सुग्रीवो राघवेणाभिपालितः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “May Śrī Rāma, skilled in the use of missiles, be eminently victorious, as well as Lakṣmaṇa, endowed with extraordinary might. Triumphant is King Sugrīva, protected on all sides by Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu. (8)

verses.text:
दासोऽहं कोसलेन्द्रस्य रामस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः।
हनूमान् शत्रुसैन्यानां निहन्ता मारुतात्मजः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “I, Hanumān, sprung from the loins of the wind-god, and destroyer of hostile armies, am a servant of Śrī Rāma of unwearied action, the lord of Kośala. (9)

verses.text:
न रावणसहस्रं मे युद्धे प्रतिबलं भवेत्।
शिलाभिश्च प्रहरतः पादपैश्च सहस्रशः॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Not even a thousand of Rāvaṇas can stand my might in combat, even as I assail them with myriad of rocks and trees. (10)

verses.text:
धर्षयित्वा पुरीं लङ्कामभिवाद्य च मैथिलीम्।
समृद्धार्थो गमिष्यामि मिषतां सर्वरक्षसाम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Destroying the city of Laṅkā and greeting Sītā, the princess of Mithilā, I shall return fully accomplished of purpose, while all the ogres stand looking on.” (11)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा महाकायश्चैत्यस्थो हरियूथपः।
ननाद भीमनिर्ह्रादो रक्षसां जनयन् भयम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: Having shouted thus while standing on the sanctuary, the colossal Hanumān, a leader of the monkey hordes, emitted a terrible thunder-like roar, causing terror to the ogres. (12)

verses.text:
तेन नादेन महता चैत्यपालाः शतं ययुः।
गृहीत्वा विविधानस्त्रान् प्रासान् खड्गान् परश्वधान्॥ १३॥
विसृजन्तो महाकाया मारुतिं पर्यवारयन्।
ते गदाभिर्विचित्राभिः परिघैः काञ्चनाङ्गदैः॥ १४॥
आजग्मुर्वानरश्रेष्ठं बाणैश्चादित्यसंनिभैः।
आवर्त इव गङ्गायास्तोयस्य विपुलो महान्॥ १५॥
परिक्षिप्य हरिश्रेष्ठं स बभौ रक्षसां गणः।
ततो वातात्मजः क्रुद्धो भीमरूपं समास्थितः॥ १६॥
प्रासादस्य महांस्तस्य स्तम्भं हेमपरिष्कृतम्।
उत्पाटयित्वा वेगेन हनूमान् मारुतात्मजः॥ १७॥
ततस्तं भ्रामयामास शतधारं महाबलः।
तत्र चाग्निः समभवत् प्रासादश्चाप्यदह्यत॥ १८॥
verses.m: Impelled by that great noise, a hundred gigantic guards posted at the sanctuary sallied forth seizing missiles of every description, as well as spears, swords and axes, and discharging them, surrounded Hanumān, son of the wind-god, from all sides. Armed with weird maces, iron clubs plated with gold and arrows shining brightly as the sun, they approached Hanumān, the foremost of monkeys. Surrounding Hanumān, that host of ogres looked like a mighty and extensive whirlpool in the stream of the Gaṅgā. The infuriated Hanumān thereupon took on a terrible aspect. Tearing up with impetuosity a pillar, decked with gold, and bristling with a hundred edges of that edifice, the great Hanumān, sprung from the loins of the wind-god and endowed with extraordinary might, then began to spin it round, so that fire was generated from it due to its attrition with other pillars and the edifice was set ablaze with it. (13—18)

verses.text:
दह्यमानं ततो दृष्ट्वा प्रासादं हरियूथपः।
स राक्षसशतं हत्वा वज्रेणेन्द्र इवासुरान्॥ १९॥
अन्तरिक्षस्थितः श्रीमानिदं वचनमब्रवीत्।
मादृशानां सहस्राणि विसृष्टानि महात्मनाम्॥ २०॥
बलिनां वानरेन्द्राणां सुग्रीववशवर्तिनाम्।
अटन्ति वसुधां कृत्स्नां वयमन्ये च वानराः॥ २१॥
verses.m: Having dispatched all the hundred ogres posted there by means of that pillar, even as Indra got rid of demons with his thunderbolt, and on seeing that monument in flames, that glorious leader of monkey hordes then proclaimed as follows, standing in airspace all the while : “Thousands of colossal and mighty leaders of monkeys, resembling me and amenable to the control of Sugrīva, have been dispatched in all directions. We as well as other monkeys are scouring the entire globe. (19—21)

verses.text:
दशनागबलाः केचित् केचिद् दशगुणोत्तराः।
केचिन्नागसहस्रस्य बभूवुस्तुल्यविक्रमाः॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Some of them are endowed with the strength of ten elephants, others are ten times as strong as the former, while still others are equal in prowess to a thousand elephants. (22)

verses.text:
सन्ति चौघबलाः केचित् सन्ति वायुबलोपमाः।
अप्रमेयबलाः केचित् तत्रासन् हरियूथपाः॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Some leaders of monkey hordes out of them are endowed with the strength of a flood, while others are as strong as the wind, while still others possess strength beyond measure. (23)

verses.text:
ईदृग्विधैस्तु हरिभिर्वृतो दन्तनखायुधैः।
शतैः शतसहस्रैश्च कोटिभिश्चायुतैरपि॥ २४॥
आगमिष्यति सुग्रीवः सर्वेषां वो निषूदनः।
नेयमस्ति पुरी लङ्का न यूयं न च रावणः।
यस्य त्विक्ष्वाकुवीरेण बद्धं वैरं महात्मना॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Surrounded by hundreds, nay, myriads, lakhs and even crores of such monkeys, Sugrīva, who is capable of destroying you all, will come here soon. Neither will this city of Laṅkā endure, nor you, ogres, nor again Rāvaṇa, by whom enmity has actually been courted with the high-souled Śrī Rāma, the hero of the House of Ikṣwāku.” (24-25)

verses.text:
संदिष्टो राक्षसेन्द्रेण प्रहस्तस्य सुतो बली।
जम्बुमाली महादंष्ट्रो निर्जगाम धनुर्धरः॥ १॥
रक्तमाल्याम्बरधरः स्रग्वी रुचिरकुण्डलः।
महान् विवृत्तनयनश्चण्डः समरदुर्जयः॥ २॥
धनुः शक्रधनुःप्रख्यं महद् रुचिरसायकम्।
विस्फारयाणो वेगेन वज्राशनिसमस्वनम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: Commanded by Rāvaṇa, the lord of ogres, Jambumālī, the eminent, mighty and ferocious son of Prahasta, who had large teeth, carried a bow and was difficult to conquer in battle, sallied forth clad in crimson and adorned with a garland of red flowers, a chaplet and brilliant earrings, and stretching with impetuosity his large bow, which resembled a rainbow, was furnished with shining arrows and which when twanged produced a sound like that of thunder and that accompanying a stroke of lightning, his eyes rolling through anger. (1—3)

verses.text:
तस्य विस्फारघोषेण धनुषो महता दिशः।
प्रदिशश्च नभश्चैव सहसा समपूर्यत॥ ४॥
verses.m: All the four quarters as well as the intermediate points as also the sky got filled all of a sudden with the thunderous twang of that bow. (4)

verses.text:
रथेन खरयुक्तेन तमागतमुदीक्ष्य सः।
हनूमान् वेगसम्पन्नो जहर्ष च ननाद च॥ ५॥
verses.m: Observing him arrived in a chariot drawn by donkeys, the celebrated Hanumān, who was full of vigour, rejoiced and roared too. (5)

verses.text:
तं तोरणविटङ्कस्थं हनूमन्तं महाकपिम्।
जम्बुमाली महातेजा विव्याध निशितैः शरैः॥ ६॥
verses.m: Jambumālī, who was endowed with extraordinary energy, pierced with sharpened arrows that great monkey, Hanumān, standing on the top of the archway. (6)

verses.text:
अर्धचन्द्रेण वदने शिरस्येकेन कर्णिना।
बाह्वोर्विव्याध नाराचैर्दशभिस्तु कपीश्वरम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: He for his part hit Hanumān, the leader of monkeys, in the mouth with an arrow with a crescent-shaped head, on the head with a single barbed shaft and in the arms with ten steel arrows. (7)

verses.text:
तस्य तच्छुशुभे ताम्रं शरेणाभिहतं मुखम्।
शरदीवाम्बुजं फुल्लं विद्धं भास्कररश्मिना॥ ८॥
verses.m: Pierced with an arrow, his well-known coppery countenance looked charming like a blown red lotus lit by a sunbeam in autumn. (8)

verses.text:
तत्तस्य रक्तं रक्तेन रञ्जितं शुशुभे मुखम्।
यथाऽऽकाशे महापद्मं सिक्तं काञ्चनबिन्दुभिः॥ ९॥
verses.m: Stained with blood, his ruddy face looked splendid like a large red lotus in the sky, sprinkled with drops of honey of a red Aśoka flower. (9)

verses.text:
चुकोप बाणाभिहतो राक्षसस्य महाकपिः।
ततः पार्श्वेऽतिविपुलां ददर्श महतीं शिलाम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: Wounded by the shafts of the ogre, the great monkey waxed wroth. Presently he sighted by his side a big rock of immense proportions. (10)

verses.text:
तरसा तां समुत्पाट्य चिक्षेप जववद् बली।
तां शरैर्दशभिः क्रुद्धस्ताडयामास राक्षसः॥ ११॥
verses.m: Tearing it up with impetuosity, the mighty monkey hurled it with vehemence. Full of rage the ogre broke it asunder with ten arrows. (11)

verses.text:
विपन्नं कर्म तद् दृष्ट्वा हनूमांश्चण्डविक्रमः।
सालं विपुलमुत्पाट्य भ्रामयामास वीर्यवान्॥ १२॥
verses.m: Uprooting a huge sal tree on seeing the aforesaid feat brought to naught, the powerful Hanumān, who was endowed with terrific prowess, began to whirl it. (12)

verses.text:
भ्रामयन्तं कपिं दृष्ट्वा सालवृक्षं महाबलम्।
चिक्षेप सुबहून् बाणाञ्जम्बुमाली महाबलः॥ १३॥
verses.m: Perceiving the monkey, who was endowed with extraordinary might, spinning the sal tree, the highly powerful Jambumālī let loose numerous shafts. (13)

verses.text:
सालं चतुर्भिश्चिच्छेद वानरं पञ्चभिर्भुजे।
उरस्येकेन बाणेन दशभिस्तु स्तनान्तरे॥ १४॥
verses.m: He rent the sal asunder with four arrows and pierced the monkey in his arms with five others, in the chest with a further dart and between the breasts with ten more. (14)

verses.text:
स शरैः पूरिततनुः क्रोधेन महता वृतः।
तमेव परिघं गृह्य भ्रामयामास वेगितः॥ १५॥
verses.m: Seizing the same iron club (which he had made use of in the very first instance), Hanumān, whose body was covered with darts and who was now overcome with violent anger, spun it with impetuosity. (15)

verses.text:
अतिवेगोऽतिवेगेन भ्रामयित्वा बलोत्कटः।
परिघं पातयामास जम्बुमालेर्महोरसि॥ १६॥
verses.m: Whirling the club with extreme velocity, full of great impetuosity as he was, Hanumān, who was superior in strength directed it against the broad chest of Jambumālī. (16)

verses.text:
तस्य चैव शिरो नास्ति न बाहू जानुनी न च।
न धनुर्न रथो नाश्वास्तत्रादृश्यन्त नेषवः॥ १७॥
verses.m: Neither could his head be discerned any more nor his arms nor his knees nor his bow nor his chariot nor the donkeys yoked to it nor the arrows placed in his quiver. (17)

verses.text:
स हतस्तरसा तेन जम्बुमाली महारथः।
पपात निहतो भूमौ चूर्णिताङ्ग इव द्रुमः॥ १८॥
verses.m: Struck with violence by that club, Jambumālī, who was an eminent chariot-warrior, dropped dead on the ground like a tree with its boughs and trunk etc., smashed. (18)

verses.text:
जम्बुमालिं सुनिहतं किंकरांश्च महाबलान्।
चुक्रोध रावणः श्रुत्वा क्रोधसंरक्तलोचनः॥ १९॥
verses.m: Rāvaṇa waxed wroth on hearing of Jambumālī as well as of the Kiṅkaras, who were endowed with extraordinary might, having been easily killed, his eyes bloodshot through anger. (19)

verses.text:
स रोषसंवर्तितताम्रलोचनः
प्रहस्तपुत्रे निहते महाबले।
अमात्यपुत्रानतिवीर्यविक्रमान्
समादिदेशाशु निशाचरेश्वरः॥ २०॥
verses.m: On Jambumālī (son of Prahasta), who was endowed with extraordinary might, having been killed, the notorious Rāvaṇa (the lord of ogres), whose coppery eyes began to roll rapidly through anger, promptly commanded the sons of his chief minister, who were endowed with surpassing virility and prowess, to march against Hanumān. (20)

verses.text:
ततस्ते राक्षसेन्द्रेण चोदिता मन्त्रिणः सुताः।
निर्ययुर्भवनात् तस्मात् सप्त सप्तार्चिवर्चसः॥ १॥
महद्बलपरीवारा धनुष्मन्तो महाबलाः।
कृतास्त्रास्त्रविदां श्रेष्ठाः परस्परजयैषिणः॥ २॥
हेमजालपरिक्षिप्तैर्ध्वजवद्भिः पताकिभिः।
तोयदस्वननिर्घोषैर्वाजियुक्तैर्महारथैः ॥ ३॥
तप्तकाञ्चनचित्राणि चापान्यमितविक्रमाः।
विस्फारयन्तः संहृष्टास्तडिद्वन्त इवाम्बुदाः॥ ४॥
verses.m: Commanded by Rāvaṇa, the ruler of ogres, the aforesaid seven sons of his chief minister—who were splendid as fire—were followed by a large army, armed with bows and endowed with extraordinary might and immeasurable prowess, and were the foremost of those trained in the science of arms and skilled in the use of missiles and were eager to excel one another in fighting, sallied forth, highly delighted, from that palace of Rāvaṇa in large chariots to which horses were yoked, were overlaid with a protective armour of gold, were surmounted by banners and decorated with smaller flags and which made a rattling sound resembling a peal of thunder, stretching their bows inlaid with refined gold and as such looking like clouds accompanied by flashes of lightning. (1—4)

verses.text:
जनन्यस्तास्ततस्तेषां विदित्वा किंकरान् हतान्।
बभूवुः शोकसम्भ्रान्ताः सबान्धवसुहृज्जनाः॥ ५॥
verses.m: Coming to know of the Kiṅkaras having been killed, their mothers alongwith their near and dear ones got confounded on account of grief and fear of further calamity. (5)

verses.text:
ते परस्परसंघर्षात् तप्तकाञ्चनभूषणाः।
अभिपेतुर्हनूमन्तं तोरणस्थमवस्थितम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: Vying with one another to take the lead, the chief minister’s sons, who were decked with ornaments of refined gold, rushed on Hanumān, who stood on the archway motionless. (6)

verses.text:
सृजन्तो बाणवृष्टिं ते रथगर्जितनिःस्वनाः।
प्रावृट्काल इवाम्भोदा विचेरुर्नैर्ऋताम्बुदाः॥ ७॥
verses.m: Discharging a hail of shafts like watery clouds during the monsoon, the aforesaid cloud in the shape of ogres rambled about, emitting a sound like a clap of thunder in the shape of the rattling of their chariots. (7)

verses.text:
अवकीर्णस्ततस्ताभिर्हनूमान् शरवृष्टिभिः।
अभवत् संवृताकारः शैलराडिव वृष्टिभिः॥ ८॥
verses.m: Covered by those showers of shafts, Hanumān became invisible even as a king of mountains is obscured by incessant showers. (8)

verses.text:
स शरान् वञ्चयामास तेषामाशुचरः कपिः।
रथवेगांश्च वीराणां विचरन् विमलेऽम्बरे॥ ९॥
verses.m: Wheeling about in the cloudless sky, that swift-footed monkey, Hanumān, eluded the shafts of those heroic ogres as well as the onrush of their chariots. (9)

verses.text:
स तैः क्रीडन् धनुष्मद्भिर्व्योम्नि वीरः प्रकाशते।
धनुष्मद्भिर्यथा मेघैर्मारुतः प्रभुरम्बरे॥ १०॥
verses.m: Sporting in the air with those warriors, each armed with a bow, the hero shone like the powerful wind-god playing in the heavens with clouds accompanied by rainbows. (10)

verses.text:
स कृत्वा निनदं घोरं त्रासयंस्तां महाचमूम्।
चकार हनुमान् वेगं तेषु रक्षःसु वीर्यवान्॥ ११॥
verses.m: Emitting a terrible roar and striking terror into that large army, the powerful Hanumān rushed on those ogres. (11)

verses.text:
तलेनाभिहनत् कांश्चित् पादैः कांश्चित् परंतपः।
मुष्टिभिश्चाहनत् कांश्चिन्नखैः कांश्चिद् व्यदारयत्॥ १२॥
verses.m: Hanumān, the scourge of his enemies, struck down some with the palm of his hand, and some more with his feet. He hit others with his fists and tore still others with his nails. (12)

verses.text:
प्रममाथोरसा कांश्चिदूरुभ्यामपरानपि।
केचित् तस्यैव नादेन तत्रैव पतिता भुवि॥ १३॥
verses.m: He crushed some with his chest and others against his thighs, while others fell on the ground at the very spot where they stood, simply at the roar of Hanumān. (13)

verses.text:
ततस्तेष्ववसन्नेषु भूमौ निपतितेषु च।
तत्सैन्यमगमत् सर्वं दिशो दश भयार्दितम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: The said sons of Rāvaṇa’s chief minister having been got rid of and fallen on the ground, that army fled in all the ten directions, stricken with fear. (14)

verses.text:
विनेदुर्विस्वरं नागा निपेतुर्भुवि वाजिनः।
भग्ननीडध्वजच्छत्रैर्भूश्च कीर्णाभवद् रथैः॥ १५॥
verses.m: Elephants trumpeted dissonantly, horses fell to the ground and the earth was strewn with chariots which had their seats, ensigns and canopies shattered. (15)

verses.text:
स्रवता रुधिरेणाथ स्रवन्त्यो दर्शिताः पथि।
विविधैश्च स्वनैर्लङ्का ननाद विकृतं तदा॥ १६॥
verses.m: Rivers were presented to the view by blood flowing on the way. Nay, Laṅkā seemed to shriek wild due to various cries uttered by its denizens. (16)

verses.text:
स तान् प्रवृद्धान् विनिहत्य राक्षसान्
महाबलश्चण्डपराक्रमः कपिः।
युयुत्सुरन्यैः पुनरेव राक्षसै-
स्तदेव वीरोऽभिजगाम तोरणम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: Having disposed of those arrogant ogres, the heroic monkey, Hanumān, who was endowed with extraordinary might and terrific prowess, sought once more the same archway, eager to give battle to other ogres. (17)

verses.text:
हतान् मन्त्रिसुतान् बुद्ध्वा वानरेण महात्मना।
रावणः संवृताकारश्चकार मतिमुत्तमाम्॥ १॥
verses.m: Coming to know of his chief minister’s sons having been killed by the colossal monkey, Rāvaṇa, who had hypocritically concealed the expression of his face giving a clue to the disposition of his mind, made a crafty resolution to renew his efforts to tame the monkey. (1)

verses.text:
स विरूपाक्षयूपाक्षौ दुर्धरं चैव राक्षसम्।
प्रघसं भासकर्णं च पञ्च सेनाग्रनायकान्॥ २॥
संदिदेश दशग्रीवो वीरान् नयविशारदान्।
हनूमद्ग्रहणेऽव्यग्रान् वायुवेगसमान् युधि॥ ३॥
verses.m: That ten-headed monster commanded five leading generals of his army, viz., Virupākṣa and Yupākṣa as well as the ogre Dūrdhara, Praghaṣa and Bhāsakarṇa, who were valiant, nay, past masters in strategy and imperturbable and approached the speed of the wind on the field of battle, to take Hanumān captive. (2-3)

verses.text:
यात सेनाग्रगाः सर्वे महाबलपरिग्रहाः।
सवाजिरथमातङ्गाः स कपिः शास्यतामिति॥ ४॥
verses.m: “March you all, O generals, taking a large army with you and accompanied by horses, chariots and elephants and let that monkey be punished. (4)

verses.text:
यत्तैश्च खलु भाव्यं स्यात् तमासाद्य वनालयम्।
कर्म चापि समाधेयं देशकालाविरोधितम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Approaching that monkey, you must surely remain alert and action should be taken by you, which is not out of harmony with time and place. (5)

verses.text:
न ह्यहं तं कपिं मन्ये कर्मणा प्रति तर्कयन्।
सर्वथा तन्महद् भूतं महाबलपरिग्रहम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Judging him by his actions, I surely do not account him a monkey. At all events he must be some great being endowed with extraordinary might. (6)

verses.text:
वानरोऽयमिति ज्ञात्वा नहि शुद्ध्यति मे मनः।
नैवाहं तं कपिं मन्ये यथेयं प्रस्तुता कथा॥ ७॥
verses.m: “My mind is surely not ready to believe that he is a monkey. I certainly do not account him a monkey as the story which is told about him shows. (7)

verses.text:
भवेदिन्द्रेण वा सृष्टमस्मदर्थं तपोबलात्।
सनागयक्षगन्धर्वदेवासुरमहर्षयः ॥ ८॥
युष्माभिः प्रहितैः सर्वैर्मया सह विनिर्जिताः।
तैरवश्यं विधातव्यं व्यलीकं किंचिदेव नः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “He may be some creature evolved for our annihilation by Indra, the ruler of gods, by virtue of his askesis. Gods, demons and eminent Ṛṣis alongwith Nāgas, Yakṣas and Gandharvas were utterly vanquished by you (the ogre army) under my command and standing by me. Something unpleasant to us need must be done by them. (8-9)

verses.text:
तदेव नात्र संदेहः प्रसह्य परिगृह्यताम्।
यात सेनाग्रगाः सर्वे महाबलपरिग्रहाः॥ १०॥
सवाजिरथमातङ्गाः स कपिः शास्यतामिति।
नावमन्यो भवद्भिश्च कपिर्धीरपराक्रमः॥ ११॥
verses.m: “It is precisely some such being: there is no doubt about it. He must be taken captive by force. March you all, O generals, taking a large army with you and accompanied by horses, chariots and elephants. Let that monkey be chastised. Nay, the monkey, who is endowed with steady prowess, should not be disregarded by you. (10-11)

verses.text:
दृष्टा हि हरयः पूर्वे मया विपुलविक्रमाः।
वाली च सह सुग्रीवो जाम्बवांश्च महाबलः॥ १२॥
नीलः सेनापतिश्चैव ये चान्ये द्विविदादयः।
नैव तेषां गतिर्भीमा न तेजो न पराक्रमः॥ १३॥
न मतिर्न बलोत्साहो न रूपपरिकल्पनम्।
महत्सत्त्वमिदं ज्ञेयं कपिरूपं व्यवस्थितम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Monkeys of immense prowess have been actually seen by me in the past, viz., Vāli alongwith Sugrīva, as well as Jāmbavān, the bear, who is endowed with extraordinary might, as also General Nīla and others such as Dwivida. Their capacity to leap, however, is not so tremendous, nor energy, nor prowess, nor intellect, nor strength and vigour, nor ability to assume different forms at will. He should be concluded to be some mighty creature drawn up in the form of a monkey. (12—14)

verses.text:
प्रयत्नं महदास्थाय क्रियतामस्य निग्रहः।
कामं लोकास्त्रयः सेन्द्राः ससुरासुरमानवाः॥ १५॥
भवतामग्रतः स्थातुं न पर्याप्ता रणाजिरे।
तथापि तु नयज्ञेन जयमाकाङ्क्षता रणे॥ १६॥
आत्मा रक्ष्यः प्रयत्नेन युद्धसिद्धिर्हि चञ्चला।
ते स्वामिवचनं सर्वे प्रतिगृह्य महौजसः॥ १७॥
समुत्पेतुर्महावेगा हुताशसमतेजसः।
रथैश्च मत्तैर्नागैश्च वाजिभिश्च महाजवैः॥ १८॥
शस्त्रैश्च विविधैस्तीक्ष्णैः सर्वैश्चोपहिता बलैः।
ततस्तु ददृशुर्वीरा दीप्यमानं महाकपिम्॥ १९॥
रश्मिमन्तमिवोद्यन्तं स्वतेजोरश्मिमालिनम्।
तोरणस्थं महावेगं महासत्त्वं महाबलम्॥ २०॥
महामतिं महोत्साहं महाकायं महाभुजम्।
तं समीक्ष्यैव ते सर्वे दिक्षु सर्वास्ववस्थिताः॥ २१॥
तैस्तैः प्रहरणैर्भीमैरभिपेतुस्ततस्ततः।
तस्य पञ्चायसास्तीक्ष्णाः सिताः पीतमुखाः शराः।
शिरस्युत्पलपत्राभा दुर्धरेण निपातिताः॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Putting forth extraordinary effort, let him be taken captive. Even all the three worlds (heaven, earth and the intermediate region) including Indra, the ruler of the three worlds, as well as gods, demons and human beings are not able to stand before you on the field of battle. Nevertheless, one’s own self must at all events be zealously protected by one who knows how to behave prudently and seeks to triumph in combat; for success in battle is uncertain indeed.” Bowing to the command of their master, all the generals, who were endowed with extraordinary energy and agility and equipped with sharp weapons of every kind and followed by all kinds of forces, and who were effulgent as fire, sallied forth in chariots as well as on the back of elephants in rut and horses of extraordinary swiftness. Thereupon the heroes for their part caught sight of the great monkey, Hanumān, who was endowed with extraordinary agility, extraordinary courage, extraordinary strength, extraordinary intelligence, extraordinary ardour, a gigantic body and mighty-arms, and who was blazing like the rising sun, encircled as he was by the rays of his glory. Immediately on perceiving him, they all, who were stationed in all quarters, assailed him with their dreadful weapons of all descriptions from every side. Five sharp and white polished steel shafts with yellow (golden) tips were dug into his head by Dūrdhara and shone like petals of lilies causing no more pain to him than lilies. (15—22)

verses.text:
स तैः पञ्चभिराविद्धः शरैः शिरसि वानरः।
उत्पपात नदन् व्योम्नि दिशो दश विनादयन्॥ २३॥
verses.m: Pierced in the head with those five arrows, the monkey leapt roaring in the sky, making all the ten directions resound thereby. (23)

verses.text:
ततस्तु दुर्धरो वीरः सरथः सज्जकार्मुकः।
किरन् शरशतैर्नैकैरभिपेदे महाबलः॥ २४॥
verses.m: Thereupon the valiant Dūrdhara, who was endowed with extraordinary might, arrived near him in his chariot, with his bow duly drawn and covered him with many hundreds of shafts. (24)

verses.text:
स कपिर्वारयामास तं व्योम्नि शरवर्षिणम्।
वृष्टिमन्तं पयोदान्ते पयोदमिव मारुतः॥ २५॥
verses.m: Continuing in the air, Hanumān kept back by means of his very roar Dūrdhara, who was raining arrows on him, even as the wind would keep back a rainy cloud at the end of the monsoon. (25)

verses.text:
अर्द्यमानस्ततस्तेन दुर्धरेणानिलात्मजः।
चकार निनदं भूयो व्यवर्धत च वीर्यवान्॥ २६॥
verses.m: Being tormented by the aforesaid Dūrdhara, the powerful Hanumān emitted a roar once more and grew immensely in size. (26)

verses.text:
स दूरं सहसोत्पत्य दुर्धरस्य रथे हरिः।
निपपात महावेगो विद्युद्राशिर्गिराविव॥ २७॥
verses.m: Bounding high into the sky, Hanumān precipitately jumped with great impetuosity on the chariot of Dūrdhara like a mass of lightning on a mountain. (27)

verses.text:
ततः स मथिताष्टाश्वं रथं भग्नाक्षकूबरम्।
विहाय न्यपतद् भूमौ दुर्धरस्त्यक्तजीवितः॥ २८॥
verses.m: Having lost his chariot, whose axle and pole had been broken and all the eight horses mangled, Dūrdhara dropped down dead on the ground. (28)

verses.text:
तं विरूपाक्षयूपाक्षौ दृष्ट्वा निपतितं भुवि।
तौ जातरोषौ दुर्धर्षावुत्पेततुररिंदमौ॥ २९॥
